macro_digital_gain.provenance: The X1E Linux machine driver explicitly describes the -3 dB Digital Volume limit as a temporary speaker-damage safety cap until active speaker protection is available. It is not currently backed by a direct Windows WSA-macro register observation.

source_provenance_gate.reason: The evolved reconstructed source no longer reproduces the production WSA-macro module identity. Runtime tracing therefore used the exact loaded production binary rather than a rebuilt module.

conclusion: The production Linux WSA macro is fully active before WSA8845 unmute and the exact runtime register transition is now captured on the canonical CPS-v3 binary. DP2 transport and startup ordering remain closed. Two producer-level parity items remain unproven against Windows: the macro Digital Volume safety cap at -3 dB and the active half-dB/gain-offset policy. Neither should be changed together with DRE/CSR; any candidate must isolate one variable and keep the rejected DRE-disabled cold-boot path off-limits until producer semantics are understood.
